result.title: Tracking Objects Through Assembly and Decomposition
result.summary: Tracking objects through transformations is essential for understanding real-world dynamics. Recent work has extended traditional object tracking to detect state changes. However, existing methods require an initial object prompt and detect only its decompositions, missing assembly events, which begin with multiple objects rather than one. We therefore introduce a prompt-free formulation of this task, where the goal is to recover all object tracks and detect both decomposition and assembly events given only a video. Our key insight is that assembly is decomposition in reverse. Building on this insight, we present Atlas, a zero-shot system that constructs and jointly reasons over forward and reverse spatiotemporal partitions to recover object tracks and their transformations. We further introduce OmniST, a benchmark with dense annotations of objects and both transformation types. On OmniST, Atlas recovers more than twice as many state changes as prior methods while remaining competitive on existing benchmarks that only evaluate decomposition.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究视频中跨越分解与组装变换的目标跟踪，提出无需初始提示的任务设定、零样本系统 Atlas（联合推理正向与逆向时空划分以恢复目标轨迹及变换事件），并构建密集标注基准 OmniST。
AI.relevance_reason: 「组装即分解的逆过程」与正逆向划分联合推理的思路，可能为 latent 状态的逆向动力学、双向状态更新与变换事件检测提供概念线索，但论文不涉及语言/VLM 推理，可迁移性需核查。
